Respected Sir,We, the undersigned victims of a large-scale employment and loan fraud, humbly submit this complaint to bring to your kind attention a matter of serious concern involving Sonix Human Capital Solutions Pvt. Ltd., headquartered at CIE IIIT-H, Vindhya C4, Gachibowli, Hyderabad, and Varthana Finance Private Limited, based in HRBR Layout, Bangalore.Background of the IssueWe were contacted by SONIX through random calls in early 2023-2025 offering job opportunities. They introduced the TAP Employment Program, which promised a salary of Rs.15,000 per month for the first 6 months and Rs.30,000 per month thereafter (including PF) and includes training and Job placement. As part of this program, they required a payment of Rs.3,02,131 which they said could be easily covered through a loan from their partner, Varthana Finance Pvt Ltd.Both SONIX and Varthana assured us thatThe loan EMI would only need to be paid after receiving our monthly salary.The EMI structure was Rs.5,525/- per month for the first 6 months, followed by Rs.15,525/- per month.Salaries would be credited before the 10th of each month.Believing in the promises made, we enrolled in good faith across multiple batches. However, after taking the loan, few months only they credited salaries, later no salaries were credited and we were not provided with proper training or any guaranteed job placement, and the loan sanction process was completed in a highly questionable manner without adequate background checks.

Trusting the caller, I clicked on the link and entered my credit card details, including the card number, CVV, and expiry date. After submitting these details, an OTP was sent to my registered mobile number. Without carefully checking the transaction details, I entered the OTP on the same website. Subsequently, an unauthorized amount was debited from my credit card. Within minutes of noticing the unauthorized transaction, I immediately raised a dispute through the SBI Card mobile application and blocked my credit card to prevent further misuse. Later, I realized that the website was fraudulent and that the link may have allowed the fraudsters to capture the information entered on the page.
